column1: # Candidate person identities across the sources in genealogies.tsv: each row
# names one person and every source/pos row that refers to them. A row whose
# note says HYPOTHESIS or "Single source" is an identity the texts do not
# state; research track 4 treats those as switches, never as facts.

column4: note
BSB footnote at Luke 3:38 gives the Greek as Enōs.
Kenan (Gen 5:9) = Cainan (Luke 3:37). Not the second Cainan of Luke 3:36.
Son of Jared; not Cain's son Enoch (Gen 4:17).
Son of Methuselah; not Cain's descendant Lamech (Gen 4:18).
Same person, different father: Arphaxad in Hebrew Gen 11:12, Cainan in Luke 3:35-36 (and LXX Gen 11). Not Judah's son Shelah (1 Chr 2:3).
Son of Serug, father of Terah. Not Abram's brother Nahor (Gen 11:26).
Spelled Abram in Gen 11:26 (renamed Abraham in Gen 17:5).
The patriarch; not Joseph's father Jacob in Matt 1:15-16.
The patriarch; not the Judah of Luke 3:30.

Luke 3:33 has no Ram in the BSB: it reads Admin and Arni between Amminadab and Hezron. Identifying Ram with Luke's Arni (or Admin) is a textual hypothesis; see the data notes. BSB footnote at Matt 1:3: Greek Aram.
Luke 3:32 prints Sala (BSB footnote: BYZ and TR Salmon). Hebrew has Salma at Ruth 4:20 and 1 Chr 2:11 (BSB footnotes).
Luke runs through David's son Nathan instead (Luke 3:31).
Abijam in 1 Kings (BSB footnote: a variant of Abijah).
BSB footnote at Matt 1:7: Greek Asaph.
Joram is a variant spelling of Jehoram (BSB footnote at 1 Chr 3:11).
Omitted by Matthew.
Omitted by Matthew. Hebrew Jehoash in 2 Kgs 11:21 (BSB footnote).
Omitted by Matthew.
Azariah = Uzziah (BSB footnotes at 1 Chr 3:12 and 2 Kgs 14:21).
BSB footnote at Matt 1:10: Greek Amōs. Not Luke's Amos (Luke 3:25).
Birth name Eliakim (2 Kgs 23:34). Omitted by Matthew, whose Josiah is the father of Jeconiah (Matt 1:11).
Jeconiah is a variant of Jehoiachin (BSB footnote at 1 Chr 3:16).

Son of Jeconiah (Matt 1:12; 1 Chr 3:17). Also named as Zerubbabel's father in Ezra 3:2, Ezra 3:8 and Hag 1:1 (the ezra_hag rows; Shealtiel is in their note, not their name column). Identity with Luke's Shealtiel son of Neri (shealtiel_luke) is a HYPOTHESIS, disputed among scholars.
Single source, listed for the reconciliation question. Son of Neri (Luke 3:27). Identity with shealtiel_matt is a HYPOTHESIS, disputed among scholars.

The post-exilic governor of the Jeconiah line: son of Shealtiel in Matt 1:12, Ezra 3:2, Ezra 3:8, Hag 1:1; son of Pedaiah in 1 Chr 3:19. Including the 1 Chronicles row is the conventional identification (same name, same royal line, same generation), not something the texts state. Identity with Luke's Zerubbabel (zerubbabel_luke) is a HYPOTHESIS, disputed among scholars.
Single source, listed for the reconciliation question. Son of Shealtiel son of Neri, father of Rhesa (Luke 3:27). Identity with zerubbabel_matt is a HYPOTHESIS, disputed among scholars.

Single source, listed for the reconciliation question. Joseph's father in Matt 1:16. Not the same name as Luke's Heli; any identification with or relation to Heli (e.g. levirate or Mary's-line theories) is a HYPOTHESIS.
Single source, listed for the reconciliation question. Joseph's father in Luke 3:23. Any identification with or relation to Matthew's Jacob is a HYPOTHESIS.
Matt 1:16 “Joseph, the husband of Mary”; Luke 3:23 “He was regarded as the son of Joseph”. Not the Josephs of Luke 3:24 and 3:30.
